findings.title: Preserve the original lightness for metadata author links
findings.body: This link previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses 70% for the light-theme branch and 30% for the dark-theme branch. That changes the existing light-theme color and makes the dark-theme text darker than intended. Keep 30% for the primary branch and use the complementary 70% for the secondary branch.

findings.title: Preserve the group-member name color
findings.body: The group-member name previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this replacement uses 50% for both theme branches. This makes the name lighter in existing light themes and loses the intended muted color in dark themes. Use 30% for the primary branch and 70% for the secondary branch.

findings.title: Do not invert the custom-message hint lightness
findings.body: This hint previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the replacement uses 30% for the primary branch and 70% for the secondary branch. That reverses the intended colors: it darkens the hint in light themes and makes it too light in dark themes. Use 70% for the primary branch and 30% for the secondary branch, as in the desktop modal rule.

findings.title: Preserve the topic-map heading color
findings.body: This heading previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the replacement uses 50% for both theme branches. It therefore changes the existing light-theme heading color and gives the dark theme the wrong tint. Keep 20% for the primary branch and use 80% for the secondary branch.

findings.title: Preserve the group-member name color
findings.body: The group-member name previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this replacement uses 50% for both theme branches. This makes the name lighter in existing light themes and loses the intended muted color in dark themes. Use 30% for the primary branch and 70% for the secondary branch.
